decisions.summary: Engine is installation/customer/domain/version/host agnostic
Minimal operator UX: target, ownership confirmation, start/resume
Automatic target classification rather than operator choosing technical mode
Runtime-discovered installation IDs, URL, keys, authority epoch
Durable idempotent transfer with preflight, single active authority, verified commit
No normal-path SSH, database edits, manual ZIP, or Emergency
Record every new decision and supersession without deleting old records
Public transfer first, then Local; phase A read-only classification
Cross-customer, multi-version, full end-to-end tests before release
Small-cafe UX for any customer, not special handling for a named cafe
Cryptographically enforced independent per-installation ownership boundaries
Fixed cafe identity and R241 as product default
Fixed Public target soknagroup.ir/public
Fixed Public source soknaspace.ir and QR path
Only R241 to R249 is an adequate acceptance matrix
Treat rebind, initial pair, and independent transfer as equivalent
Force operator to use DB/cPanel/manual emergency flow
Small-cafe product means the named Sokna cafe only

Target identity requires Ed25519 proof tied to exact local/target/operation AND independently authenticated owner approval. Nonce must be durably single-use before any mutation. A verified proof alone never authorizes cutover.
decisions.reason: Prevent cross-customer/host impersonation, replay, and false activation from self-signed target responses
decisions.acceptance: R252 signature and owner grant tests plus future transactional nonce ledger tests and authenticated admin E2E
decisions.implementation_status: PHASE_B_QA_PARTIAL: Ed25519 destination signature and Local-only HMAC owner-grant verification tested; authenticated owner consent endpoint, key custody and durable nonce ledger NOT IMPLEMENTED

decisions.summary: Record generic Public migration ownership challenges and approvals in a transactional per-installation authorization ledger with strictly single-use nonce and a one-active-operation slot; never treat claim as cutover.
decisions.reason: Prevent duplicate grants, cross-customer collision, retry loops, and concurrent transfer races while preserving existing Local/Public state.
decisions.acceptance: R253 isolated MariaDB 11.4 transactional tests plus future concurrent worker and end-to-end authenticated owner approval tests
decisions.implementation_status: R253_QA_LEDGER: transactional storage, verified MAC+signature acceptance, duplicate blocking and claim-once tested against disposable MariaDB; not registered as a production migration, owner approval UI/API and cutover not implemented

decisions.summary: Destination owner approval must come from an authenticated administrator scoped to that exact Public installation with same-origin CSRF protection. A freshly installed Public without staff projections requires a separate owner-login/bootstrap path in standard setup; it must never be silently approved. Per-instance signing keys live outside public webroot with least-privilege storage.
decisions.reason: R254 QA found fresh independent Public may have no projected staff admin; trusting a browser field or reusing an unrelated installation session would allow impersonation. Protected per-instance Ed25519 key material and authenticated owner access are prerequisites.
decisions.acceptance: R254 43 isolated tests, production onboarding and end-to-end fresh Public owner login yet to be implemented; key ACL and concurrent key initialization to be tested on real Windows and hosts.
decisions.implementation_status: R254_QA_PARTIAL: pure Public admin consent guard with CSRF/session/Origin checks, restricted file key store, and 43 green tests. NO endpoint, owner bootstrap session, PKCE handoff or cutover.

decisions.summary: The owner of a new independent Public installation authenticates against its own Public instance identity, NOT a Local installation identity that may not yet be paired. Standard setup stages a one-time short-lived claim from a trusted installer; owner sets a strong password and receives a short server-side session. Never bootstrap ownership from an anonymous HTTP request, never use Emergency credentials as the normal path, never conflate Public owner confirmation with Local cutover authority.
decisions.reason: R254's projected staff session is impossible on a genuinely unpaired Public; conflating Local and Public identities breaks universal migration and may cause cross-customer scope errors.
decisions.acceptance: R255 real MariaDB fresh-owner bootstrap tests, multi-customer consent binding, login lockout and one-use claim tests; future installer-owned claim/UI and E2E tests required.
decisions.implementation_status: R255_QA_PARTIAL: instance-scoped bootstrap/account/session service and independent owner consent bridge; no trusted installer wiring, no HTTP endpoint, no Local signed grant or cutover.

decisions.summary: A Public destination administrator can only be recognized through an already-projected staff session whose installation_id equals the Local installation being moved.
decisions.reason: Applicable only to already-paired Public. Fresh independent Public owner must be scoped to its own Public instance and independently authorize the signed Local challenge.

decisions.summary: Public migration features must be integrated and tested against the actual immutable release payload and its full versioned migration catalog, not a shorter legacy source tree. Public owner setup occurs inside the normal authenticated install flow and obtains an instance identity independent of Local; signing keys must be outside the effective document root. The owner HTTP API remains fail-closed and cannot create setup claims or authorize cutover.
decisions.reason: R256 source audit found apps/public had 3 schema files while R249/35IC real operator release contains 8 migrations and 228 payload files. A generic legacy patch could break production or omit accepted changes.
decisions.acceptance: Pinned 35IC ZIP sha256 and 228-byte-content checks; 8 migrations retained byte-identically plus new forward-only migration 0009; disposable MariaDB install/login/consent proof; independent CI test for upgrade/preexisting owner and real host qualification before release.
decisions.implementation_status: R256 QA overlay candidate only, exact R249 source pinned. Production deployment and real multi-tenant migration/cutover NO-GO.

decisions.summary: Treat the 3-migration apps/public source tree as sufficient authoritative source for extending the currently deployed 35IC/R249 Public.
decisions.reason: Source-of-truth mismatch: actual R249 release has 8 migrations, protected Emergency ownership and a different setup/kernel implementation.

decisions.summary: An already-installed Public can activate its independent site-owner credential ONLY via a live authenticated administrator of the sole active Local installation on that Public. Zero/multiple installations or invalid staff sessions fail closed; no automatic owner claim or DB reset. A signed destination-owner consent receipt and explicit authenticated Local administrator confirmation are both required before one-time Local ledger approval; neither authorizes cutover.
decisions.reason: Most users update an existing Public rather than clean-install. Earlier R255/R256 setup-only owner creation otherwise strands them. Separate Public ownership from Local authority and prevent cross-tenant takeover.
decisions.acceptance: Real MariaDB existing-site owner upgrade gate and signed receipt/Local admin MAC ledger; no rollout until R249-source integration, secure owner UI, upgrade tests, trusted Local session adapter, cutover/fencing and real host tests.
decisions.implementation_status: R257 Q/A classes and signed ledger unit integration; not exposed in installed Public/Local endpoint, no production migrations or order intake changes.

decisions.summary: Independent Public owner credentials can only be established during fresh clean install, so an existing Public must be reinstalled or use Emergency manually.
decisions.reason: R257 supports a guarded existing-site admin activation path; installation or database deletion is not required.

decisions.summary: Public replacement/recovery is Local-authoritative and intentionally minimal: the new Public must have zero live or pending guest orders before association; the OLD Public need not be reachable. Do not transfer its database, pending-only orders, media or historical state. After trusted owner approval and simple safe pairing, existing Local-to-Public synchronization re-publishes catalog, media, staff access and projections. Orders already received by Local are preserved. If old Public-only orders were never delivered to Local, they may be unrecoverable; present a single explicit acknowledgement. Keep new guest intake inactive until initial normal sync/health succeeds, preserve Local binding on pre-commit failure, and avoid simultaneous active pairing. Do not implement full Public backfill, order reconciliation, data snapshots or general-purpose resumable migration for this workflow.
decisions.reason: Operator explicitly narrowed the product to replace an inaccessible or failed Public quickly. Overbuilding a transfer/backfill/reconciliation engine would repeat update-engine complexity and cannot recover unreachable old Public data.
decisions.acceptance: A fresh or otherwise empty Public on arbitrary HTTPS root/subfolder can be owner-confirmed, paired, seeded via existing Local sync and enabled. Verify zero active/pending destination orders and that Local remains unchanged if setup or first sync fails. Show one clear warning for old-Public-only orders. No dependency on old-Public connectivity; no transfer of media/orders from old Public. Keep one active Local pairing and correct menu/QR routing separately.
decisions.implementation_status: R261 REAL Q/A PASS: actual independent HTTPS Public owner consent and Local administrator approval, fresh Public Pair, seeded real Local 135-item/24-image full sync, guest order delivered back into actual Local orders table, one connection outage and resume with old Local binding unchanged until sync/commit; GitHub https://github.com/mobaraki20/SoknaCafeV3/actions/runs/43825524618. Production NO-GO pending byte-preserving merge onto real R241/231FA+ Local 593 files/81 migrations, Local migration 0082, and official native Windows/Public installer qualification.
